content.text:
Based on my research, Mistral's official Code Interpreter documentation ([Code Interpreter | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/agents/agent-tools/code_interpreter)) and the [Known limitations](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations) page do **not** specify a fixed timeout value or documented behavior for what happens when executed code exceeds a time limit.

What the docs do confirm:
- Code Interpreter runs code in an isolated container via the Conversations/Agents API (not available in the Chat Completions API).
- It's used for tasks like data analysis, plotting, and code validation.

There is a separate, distinct product — **Vibe Code Web** (Mistral's cloud coding sandbox) — that does publish explicit timeout/lifecycle rules (inactivity timeouts, session length caps), documented at [Limits and lifecycle | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/limits-and-lifecycle) and [Sandbox environment | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/sandbox-environment). But this is not the same feature as the Agents/Conversations API "Code Interpreter" tool, so I can't confirm those numbers apply to it.

**Bottom line:** I could not find a documented timeout limit (or exceed-timeout behavior) specifically for the Code Interpreter agent tool. If this is important for your implementation (e.g., handling long-running executions gracefully), I'd recommend either testing empirically with a deliberately slow script, or contacting Mistral support/checking their changelog, since this may simply be undocumented.

Sources:
- [Code Interpreter | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/agents/agent-tools/code_interpreter)
- [Known limitations | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations)
- [Limits and lifecycle | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/limits-and-lifecycle)
- [Sandbox environment | Mistral Docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/sandbox-environment)
